item.title: Trilateral Summit Planned as Trade and Borders Shift: On Air, November 15, 2026
item.description:
An Israeli airstrike killed Samir Mahmoud Hassan Abu Younis, who served as the commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis. Both the Israeli military and Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades confirmed the death of the 53-year-old commander. Gaza civil defence officials received the body and reported that two other people sustained injuries in the strike. Abu Younis led the brigade for approximately two months following the death of his predecessor, Nael Abu Obeid, on September 15.
United States President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping plan to hold a trilateral meeting on Thursday, November 19, 2026, in Shenzhen, China. The White House and Moscow confirmed the gathering on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. The session marks the first joint three-way meeting among the leaders of the three nuclear-armed powers. A White House spokeswoman announced the meeting details on Friday.
Police and protesters clashed in Manila on Sunday as the forty-ninth Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit opened. Law enforcement officers detained approximately three hundred protesters following a demonstration march in Muntinlupa City. Separate groups gathered at Liwasang Bonifacio to voice opposition to the proposed Pax Silica initiative and policies of United States President Donald Trump. Malacañang urged demonstrators not to damage the national reputation during the international meetings.
Prime Minister Mark Carney announced on Saturday that Canada and the Philippines successfully concluded negotiations on a free-trade-agreement targeting formal signing by 2027. Speaking in Manila, Carney stated that the pact will eliminate over ninety percent of tariff lines across sectors spanning from agriculture to artificial intelligence. Carney also pledged up to five hundred sixty million dollars over four years to the Tropical Forests Forever Facility. He noted that separate trade discussions with the United States are making progress.
Estonia will close all border crossing points with Russia starting December 1 after security forces thwarted an attempted sabotage attack on a defense company. Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna announced the closure following evidence that the Russian GRU military intelligence service ordered an arson and explosives strike on drone manufacturer Threod Systems in Viimsi. Estonian authorities detained eight residents of Latvia overnight on Saturday in connection with the operation.
Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Bryan Bedford stated that United States airline operations should return to normal by the end of Sunday following a nationwide ground stop that lasted over four hours on Friday. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy attributed the failure to networking equipment and copper-to-fiber wire replacement work. Officials confirmed that no cyberattack or nefarious activity caused the system disruption. Duffy estimated that all residual delays will resolve entirely by the end of Monday.
Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu renewed his call for a national unity government with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot on Saturday. In a video statement, Netanyahu argued that a coalition is necessary to eliminate the Iranian threat. Eisenkot dismissed the proposal as a political spin move designed to delay government formation. In the October 27 election, Eisenkot's four-party bloc won forty-eight seats while Netanyahu's bloc secured fifty-three seats in the one-hundred-twenty-member Knesset.
The Port of New Orleans filed a one million dollar lawsuit in federal court to seize the asphalt tanker Atlantic Asphalt following a collision with the river cruise ship American Heritage on the Mississippi River.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: Rubio Attacks ICC While US Forces Repel Drones: On Air, November 14, 2026
item.description:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticized the International Criminal Court during an address on Friday at the Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention in Washington, D.C. Rubio dismissed international law as a tool of global elites and warned the tribunal against enforcing rules that the United States does not recognize. He compared the United States rejecting the court to a Roman general commanding forces not to quote laws to men with swords. Independent and international outlets such as Truthout emphasized the separate submission by human rights advocates at the Hague calling for arrest warrants for President Donald Trump and Marco Rubio.
New York City officials are examining whether unapproved plans to expand a construction project contributed to the collapse of an adjacent apartment building on Bedford Avenue in Brooklyn. The building collapse on Bedford Avenue killed eight people, including two children aged 9 and 10, and injured 18 others. The Brooklyn District Attorney's Office launched a criminal investigation into the collapse. Records from the New York City Department of Buildings show the collapsed building had 98 open violations.
President Donald Trump has informed senior national security advisers in recent days that he may hold off on launching new military strikes against Iran if the United States faces no further provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen. President Donald Trump launched a military conflict involving the United States and Israel against Iran in February. The United Nations reports that at least 25 seafarers have been killed in and around the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began. Polling indicates that the war has incurred political costs for the Republican Party following the midterm elections.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth awarded the Joint Service Commendation Medal to Specialist Thomas Iglesias of the 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, following an encounter at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Virginia. Video recorded on Veterans Day, November 11, showed the Army sentinel reprimanding Hegseth and his entourage after a member of the group talked and laughed on the monument's steps. The Pentagon stated that Hegseth welcomed the regiment to the Pentagon, where he presented the decoration. Representative Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Hegseth over the military conflict with Iran.
Demonstrators repeatedly interrupted House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries during a panel discussion at the What's Next Democratic conference in Denver, Colorado. While speaking alongside moderator Jessica Tarlov, Jeffries addressed party plans to reverse Medicaid cuts and extend Affordable Care Act tax credits when audience members shouted objections. Hecklers demanded action on Medicare for All and the Green New Deal, shouted for the impeachment of President Donald Trump, and labeled Jeffries a liar and a traitor. An online petition opposing Jeffries's bid for House Speaker accumulated over 1.1 million signatures.
SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its megarocket system from its South Texas base, achieving orbit while failing in an attempt to catch the lower-stage booster. The flight lifted off at 4:47 p.m. local time, carrying 26 Starlink satellites into orbit. Following stage separation, the Super Heavy booster experienced a guidance, navigation and control issue near the end of its descent, prompting flight controllers to order a diversion to the Gulf of Mexico. The booster automatically diverted to the water after losing a single engine out of 33 during the burn phase.
U.S. Central Command confirmed that American forces intercepted two one-way attack drones launched by Iran toward Bahrain, resulting in no casualties or damage.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: US Envoys Meet Putin While Middle East Clashes Escalate: On Air, November 13, 2026
item.description:
President Donald Trump directed Vice President JD Vance to target alleged corruption and crime in Democratic-controlled cities and states. President Trump stated that the United States does not need to pursue a deal with Iran. The directive follows criticism from Vice President Vance, who attributed Republican midterm election losses to the military conflict involving Iran. Senator John Kennedy criticized the vice president for blaming election results on that war.
A car explosion on Friday in southern Moscow critically injured Sergei Zavorotnyi, an adviser to former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, according to Russia's Investigative Committee. Zavorotnyi was hospitalized with injuries including the loss of his left arm and placed in a coma, while Russian authorities opened a criminal case on attempted murder charges. The attack followed a car bombing in St Petersburg on Thursday that killed a military serviceman in his vehicle.
Speaking at the What's Next conference in Denver on Thursday, Texas Senator-elect James Talarico called on his party to make the final two years of President Donald Trump's term productive through bipartisan cooperation. Several newly elected Democratic officials warned against prioritizing congressional investigations over legislative results.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated during a CNBC interview on Friday that the Treasury, Defense, State departments, and the Office of the United States Trade Representative supported adding the Singapore-based company Megaspeed to a trade blacklist for months. Bessent noted that the Commerce Department controlled the process and delayed the action. The remarks followed reports of tensions in the administration over enforcement of export controls on artificial intelligence chips.
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced that its aerospace force targeted and destroyed a United States early-warning radar system in Bahrain on Friday in retaliation for a United States airstrike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik. The United States military Central Command denied that the radar had been destroyed, stating that forces intercepted two one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain without any reported casualties or damage. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported ongoing speed restrictions on the Starshield satellite system affecting military operations.
Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot accused caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of fueling a campaign of delegitimization against the country's Arab minority. Eisenkot stated on X that Arab citizens of Israel represent an integral part of the Israeli story and condemned attempts to marginalize them collectively. Netanyahu and his allies criticized Arab party leaders for refusing to describe Hamas as a terror group following the October attacks.
Former Representative Mary Peltola gained 5,000 newly counted votes and extended her lead over Senator Dan Sullivan to 5,800 votes in the uncalled Alaska Senate race. With 88 percent of the vote reported, Peltola holds 121,487 votes to Sullivan's 117,512. Peltola's lead now exceeds the votes received by independent candidate Dan J. Sullivan, who is pulling 4,199 votes, or 1.7 percent of the total. An Alaska Superior Court judge denied a request from the Peltola campaign for records of rejected absentee ballots.
The International Atomic Energy Agency expressed concern in a confidential report circulated to member states regarding an uninspected uranium enrichment plant in Isfahan, Iran. The Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant was declared to the United Nations nuclear watchdog last year, but the agency stated it does not know the exact location, operational status, or whether the site contains nuclear material.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.
